title: El Torovenado
goal: Work out that the costumes are mocking somebody specific
culture: Torovenado is satire in costume, and every mask in it is somebody in particular — the mayor, the priest, the police, the crowd itself. It is a protected licence to say out loud what is not otherwise said, and the even-handedness is what protects it.

beats.es: (Pasa un hombre disfrazado de algo que le resulta muy familiar.)
beats.en: Are they making fun of someone?
beats.good: Burlarse is to mock. The costumes are not decoration — every one of them is a person, and the crowd knows which.
Two words, and the answer will be a name you now recognise, because you live here.

beats.es: De ese de ahí, el gordo... del alcalde, pues.
beats.good: The mayor, in a mask, in a parade, in front of the whole town. This is a protected tradition of saying out loud what is not said the rest of the year.

beats.es: Aquí nadie se salva. Ni el cura, ni la policía, ni nosotros.
beats.good: Nadie se salva — nobody is spared. Not the mayor, not the priest, not the people watching, and that even-handedness is the entire licence the day runs on.
